correctness.rationale: A_v counts ancestor antichains in descendant subtree: choose v alone, or independently select antichains in child subtrees. Every general-position subset is either such an antichain, or has exactly one selected vertex p that is ancestor of another; all remaining selected vertices must be contained in one child subtree T_v of p and must be a nonempty ancestor antichain. Any other selected ancestor, a selected vertex outside that subtree, or two comparable descendants would put three selected vertices on a geodesic. The oriented edge p→v is uniquely determined. Conversely every {p}∪B of this form is general-position, so the disjoint weighted count yields the formula. Postorder computing A_v is O(|V|) algebraic gates; expansion has potentially exponentially many monomials and is not claimed polynomial output size. Fresh independent Prüfer-tree direct geodesic subset enumeration for every labeled tree n=1..6 reproduced the complete polynomial for several roots. Infinite theorem is the structural disjoint decomposition.

originality.rationale: The 2024 foundational General Position Polynomials source gives general inclusion-exclusion over maximal general-position sets and exact specific families including paths/brooms, but not the all-tree ancestor-antichain local-edge identity and efficient multivariate circuit. Related Resultary entries treat spiders or windmill graphs, not all arbitrary trees. General rooted antichain recursion itself is classical; its specific disjoint GP-set decomposition is the substantive claim.
residual_risks: Equivalent all-tree recurrence may be known under convex independence / geodesic convexity or antichain-generating functions without GP-polynomial terminology.
Arithmetic gate count is not a bit-complexity or expanded-monomial bound.

value.rationale: Classifies all coefficients of a natural graph invariant over all trees, replacing expensive maximal-set inclusion-exclusion with a small tree arithmetic circuit. Root independence follows from the intrinsic GP polynomial and the proof. Useful for exact tree enumeration and comparisons, independent of settled scalar maximum GP size.
